Large Language Models

Large Language Models have fundamentally changed software.

Advanced 10 weeks 50 contact hours Live + recorded
Enrol / enquire → View the week-by-week syllabus

Overview

Large Language Models have fundamentally changed software. This course gives you a deep, engineering-level understanding of how LLMs work — from Transformer internals to fine-tuning open-source models, building RAG pipelines, and deploying LLM-powered applications in production.

The course runs for 10 weeks with 50 contact hours of live, instructor-led sessions — in our Chennai classroom at Rajakilpakkam, near Tambaram, or online across India. Every session is recorded for enrolled students, every module is taught by a practising AI engineer, and you receive a Data Science Academia certificate on completion.

Is this course for you?

  • Developers building LLM applications — retrieval (RAG), agents and assistants
  • Deep-learning and NLP learners who want to understand Transformers end to end
  • Technical teams evaluating which LLM approach suits their product

What you'll learn

6 learning outcomes
  • Explain the Transformer architecture at the implementation level
  • Fine-tune open-weight LLMs (Llama, Qwen, Mistral) with LoRA, QLoRA and DPO
  • Build production RAG pipelines with vector databases
  • Build tool-using LLM agents with LangGraph, LlamaIndex and MCP
  • Evaluate LLMs systematically and mitigate hallucination
  • Deploy cost-efficient LLM APIs with caching and rate control

Week-by-week syllabus

10 weeks · 60 topics
Week 1

Transformer Architecture Deep Dive
  • Attention mechanism — query, key, value from first principles
  • Scaled dot-product attention and softmax temperature
  • Multi-head attention — parallel attention across subspaces
  • Positional encoding — sinusoidal and RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding)
  • Feed-forward sublayer, LayerNorm and residual connections
  • Encoder vs decoder vs encoder-decoder architectures
Week 2

Autoregressive LLMs — GPT and Beyond
  • From GPT-1 to current frontier models — scaling laws and emergent abilities
  • Autoregressive language modelling — next-token prediction
  • Tokenisation — BPE, WordPiece and SentencePiece
  • Context window, KV-cache and attention complexity
  • Frontier model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini) — chat, tool calling and structured outputs
  • Sampling strategies — temperature, top-k, top-p, beam search
Week 3

BERT & Encoder-Based Models
  • BERT pre-training — Masked LM and Next Sentence Prediction
  • Fine-tuning BERT for classification, NER and QA
  • RoBERTa — removing NSP, dynamic masking
  • DistilBERT — knowledge distillation for 40% smaller model
  • Sentence-BERT — semantic embeddings for similarity tasks
  • DeBERTa, ELECTRA — modern BERT improvements
Week 4

Open-Source LLMs
  • Open-weight model families — Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Gemma, Mistral and gpt-oss
  • Architecture choices — grouped-query attention, sliding-window attention, mixture-of-experts
  • Small language models (Phi, Gemma, small Qwen) for constrained environments
  • Running LLMs locally with Ollama — quantised GGUF models
  • HuggingFace model hub — loading, running and inspecting models
  • Benchmarks and leaderboards — MMLU-Pro, GPQA, SWE-bench, LMArena; why older benchmarks saturate
Week 5

Prompt Engineering
  • Zero-shot, one-shot and few-shot prompting
  • Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting — reasoning step by step
  • Self-consistency — sampling multiple chains and voting
  • Reasoning models and test-time compute — when to use them instead of chain-of-thought prompting
  • ReAct — reasoning and acting with tool use
  • System prompts, role prompting and prompt injection risks
Week 6

Fine-Tuning LLMs
  • When to fine-tune vs prompt engineer vs RAG
  • Full fine-tuning vs preference tuning (DPO) — cost and dataset requirements
  • Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) — overview of strategies
  • LoRA — low-rank decomposition of weight updates
  • QLoRA — quantised LoRA for 4-bit fine-tuning on consumer GPUs
  • Building an instruction-tuning dataset and training with Unsloth
Week 7

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • RAG architecture — indexing, retrieval and generation pipeline
  • Document chunking strategies — fixed size, recursive, semantic
  • Embedding models — OpenAI, Sentence-BERT, BGE, E5
  • Vector databases — Pinecone, ChromaDB, Weaviate, Qdrant
  • Hybrid search — keyword (BM25) plus vector similarity; HNSW indexing
  • Advanced RAG: HyDE, reranking with Cohere, self-RAG
Week 8

Agents & Orchestration — LangChain, LangGraph & LlamaIndex
  • LangChain 1.0 essentials — chat models, prompt templates, tools and structured output
  • LangGraph — stateful agent graphs, memory and persistence
  • Tool-using agents and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) — web search, code execution, custom tools
  • LlamaIndex — document indexing, query engines and chat engines
  • Custom retrieval pipelines with LlamaIndex routers
  • Building a multi-document Q&A chatbot end to end
Week 9

LLM Evaluation & Safety
  • Reference-based metrics — BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore
  • LLM-as-a-judge and evaluation tooling — Ragas, DeepEval
  • Hallucination benchmarks — TruthfulQA, FEVER, HaluEval
  • Bias and fairness evaluation — StereoSet, WinoBias
  • Prompt injection, jailbreaking and red-teaming basics
  • Constitutional AI and RLHF — aligning models with human preferences
Week 10

Production LLM Systems
  • API design for LLM services — streaming, SSE and WebSockets
  • Caching — provider prompt caching and semantic caching
  • Rate limiting, cost tracking and token budgeting
  • Serving open models with vLLM — quantisation, speculative decoding, continuous batching
  • Monitoring LLM applications — logging, tracing with LangSmith
  • Capstone: deploy a domain-specific LLM assistant with RAG, memory and a Gradio interface

Questions about Large Language Models

7 answers
Do I need prior experience to join the Large Language Models course?
Deep Learning course or strong familiarity with Transformer architecture. Python proficiency essential. New to the subject? Start with Deep Learning or Natural Language Processing first.
How long is the Large Language Models course?
10 weeks with 50 contact hours of live, instructor-led sessions — about 5 hours of class a week, plus practice on your own.
Can I take Large Language Models online, or only in Chennai?
Both. Classes run live in our Chennai classroom at Rajakilpakkam, near Tambaram, and online for learners anywhere in India. Every session is recorded so enrolled students can replay it.
Will I receive a certificate?
Yes. Complete the course and its project work to receive a Data Science Academia certificate of completion that you can add to your CV and LinkedIn profile.
Which tools will I use in the Large Language Models course?
You work hands-on with Python, HuggingFace Transformers, LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, ChromaDB, Pinecone, vLLM, FastAPI and Ollama. We help you set everything up in the first session.
What can I do after completing Large Language Models?
The skills from Large Language Models are used in roles such as LLM / Generative AI Engineer, AI Application Developer and Machine Learning Engineer. Most roles also expect a portfolio of projects, which this course helps you start. To keep building, learners usually continue with Generative AI or MLOps & Model Deployment.
What are the fees, and when does the next batch start?
Fees and batch dates depend on the delivery mode you choose. Enquire online, WhatsApp +91 91764 98814 or email info@datascienceacademia.in for current pricing and the next start date — we reply within one business day. You can also book a free, no-commitment trial session.
